frozen_before: any C5 analysis or rollout exists

the_gap_c4_left.what_c4_tested: reversal across six binary STATE partitions (score stratum, carrier present, home threatened, forward commitment, carrier pressure, defender tag availability)
the_gap_c4_left.result: C4_NO_REVERSAL -- zero reversals in any single policy across 1,260 states
the_gap_c4_left.what_c4_never_tested: reversal across OPPONENTS. Opponent identity is excluded from legal_context by design, because a router cannot see it, so it was never a C4 partition.
the_gap_c4_left.why_that_exclusion_does_not_settle_the_d: Whether a strategic tradeoff EXISTS in the world and whether it is ROUTABLE from legal context are different questions. C4 answered a routability-shaped question. C5 answers the existence-shaped one.
the_gap_c4_left.this_is_not_widening_the_c4_partition_li: C4's freeze prohibits adding a seventh partition to keep searching for a C4 pass. C5 is a different question with its own verdict, and its outcome cannot rehabilitate C4.

opponent_identity_usage.may_be_used_for: grouping states to test whether demand exists
opponent_identity_usage.may_never_be_used_as: a policy input, a router feature, or a training signal
opponent_identity_usage.why_recorded: the whole point of the exclusion in legal_context is that a deployed router cannot observe it; using it here measures the world, not the agent

question: Does the ranking of two legal team responses reverse between two opponents?
target_pattern: against opponent A, response R1 beats R2 by >= delta; against opponent B, R2 beats R1 by >= delta; both CIs excluding zero

inherited_unchanged_from_c4.support_minima: 30 states per response pair per side
inherited_unchanged_from_c4.statistics: episode-clustered bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 12345, LCB95 = q_0.025
inherited_unchanged_from_c4.replication: same opponent pair, same response pair, same direction, in >= 2 of 3 G0 policies

opponent_pairs.rule: all unordered pairs from the admitted mixture
opponent_pairs.multiplicity_declared: 21 opponent pairs x response pairs are examined without correction, by design. C5 is a DISCOVERY screen; a pass earns confirmation on a fresh block, never a claim on its own.

discovery.status: REPLAY of the block C4 already consumed
discovery.why_replay_is_legitimate: the frozen G0 policies are deterministic, so this regenerates the SAME natural trajectories C4 analysed. No new information is consumed; only the grouping of already-visited states changes. Precedent: the C3 Stage-2a replay under c913c1e's predecessor.

confirmation.rule: tests only the single top-ranked candidate from discovery

C5_PASS.condition: at least one (opponent pair, response pair) reverses per the criterion in >= 2/3 policies on discovery AND replicates on the confirmation block
C5_PASS.does_not_establish: that the demand is routable from legal context
C5_PASS.mandatory_next_step: the observability test -- oracle-selector gain vs legal-selector gain -- before any O-oracle training. Demand that no legal observation can reach cannot support a router.

C5_NO_REVERSAL.condition: no opponent pair satisfies the criterion
C5_NO_REVERSAL.meaning: no response tradeoff exists across the admitted opponent mixture either, under this utility and delta
C5_NO_REVERSAL.action: STOP searching within the existing opponent set. The remaining legitimate route is constructing NEW strategic demand -- opponent families designed so that what helps against one hurts against another -- under a new preregistration, with the tradeoff still DISCOVERED rather than assumed.

prohibited: using opponent identity as a policy or router input
training any oracle on a C5_PASS before the observability test
adding partitions or opponents after seeing results
adjusting delta, support minima or the replication rule
treating a C5_PASS as rehabilitating C4 or O3
claiming a task-outcome tradeoff from a carrier_survival screen
immutability: After any C5 number exists, none of the above may change.
